en.title: Amazon OA #311: Next Perfect String
en.description: A string is perfect if no two adjacent characters are the same. Given a string s of lowercase English letters (s itself may or may not be perfect), find the smallest perfect string that has the same length as s and is lexicographically strictly greater than s. If none exists, output -1.
en.input: One line containing the string s. 1≤length of s≤200000, lowercase English letters only.
en.output: Output the answer string; if none exists, output -1.
en.explanation:
Example 1: s="abzzzcd". The z right after the prefix abz equals it, so the string must increase at an index ≤2; the z at index 2 cannot increase any further, so change the b at index 1 to c and fill the rest with the smallest alternating string ababa, giving "acababa".
Example 2: s="zzab". The z at index 0 cannot increase, and increasing index 1 would also require going past z, so no answer exists; output -1.
Example 3: s="abab" is already perfect, and the smallest perfect string strictly greater than it is "abac".
hints: The prefix kept in the answer must itself be perfect, so it cannot extend past the first place where two adjacent characters are equal.
Starting from the longest prefix that can be kept, search leftward for a position that can be increased.
After the increased position, fill the rest by alternating a and b.
